description:
A Go compiler, code editor and learning workspace for iPhone and iPad. Write, build, run, test, vet and format Go on your device with the bundled Go 1.27.1 toolchain, even offline.

BUILD REAL PROJECTS
• Edit Go and go.mod with syntax highlighting, completion and keyboard shortcuts.
• Follow compiler diagnostics to their source line and column, and inspect per-case test results.
• Import public GitHub repositories from the app or share sheet, folders from Files, or exported archives.
• Navigate nested folders and grouped module dependencies. Organize projects with folders, tags, favorites and file-name search.
• Download compatible pure-Go modules through the official Go proxy and checksum database. Vendored sources build offline.
• Continue working while downloads run, inspect meaningful failures and retry from Output. Clear downloaded packages from saved user projects without deleting your code.

LEARN AND PRACTICE
• Explore 145 teaching lessons in 20 units, plus 22 prediction challenges. Topics include core Go, structs, collections, interfaces, errors, modules, generics, concurrency and the standard library.
• Read 98 worked lessons, including 19 architecture and eight clean-code lessons, all 23 classic design patterns and six concurrent Go patterns. Compare architecture choices for tools, domain-rich apps and services with editorial suitability ratings.
• Around Go now has 25 practical lessons: Bash commands and scripts, Git, Go tools, curl, Linux services, Docker, Compose, Podman and Kubernetes.
• Follow Kubernetes contexts, manifests, dry-run and diff, logs and events, Service routing, configuration, probes, scaling and rollback.
• Use compiler-judged exercises, 69 original visual guides, 56 design diagrams, practical notes and primary references.
• Read highlighted Go, shell, Dockerfile and YAML examples. Expand code to full screen; embedded examples scroll with the lesson.
• Match learned concepts in Review, finish multi-round sessions, and work through saved mistakes with three-answer questions and immediate explanations. Progress survives reopening the app.
• Explore Idiom Coach, runnable Concurrency Lab scenarios, Go-generated PNGs and local HTML/CSS/JavaScript previews.

MADE FOR YOUR SCREEN
Keep files, code and a resizable results dock together on iPad. Use collapsible Files and panel switching on iPhone, with compact landscape controls and room for code. On supported iPhone Duo systems, expanded and folded layouts adapt to the display; laptop posture keeps code or Terminal above the horizontal fold and keyboard or results below it.
Choose your theme and text size, optional keep-awake during builds and downloads, and Face ID or device-passcode locking.

PRIVACY AND LIMITS
One paid download. No subscription, app account, analytics or advertising trackers. Projects and learning progress stay local; a chosen Files or iCloud library follows your provider's sync rules. Package search, downloads, imports and external links use the network.

Compiled Go runs in a bounded WebAssembly/WASI sandbox with one writable project directory and no network access. cgo and arbitrary shell commands are unsupported; the terminal exposes app-supported commands. Bash, Git, Docker, Kubernetes and native service examples are learning material for your own development environment. WebKit website previews may load remote resources included by your project.

promotionalText: Code, run and test Go offline. Learn with 145 lessons, deeper Go architecture and clean code, all 23 classic design patterns and practical developer commands.
whatsNew:
• Added 53 worked readings on Go architecture, clean code and design patterns. The course now includes 145 teaching lessons in 20 units, with 98 readings and 22 separate prediction challenges.
• Explore 19 architecture lessons: monoliths, layers, hexagonal and Clean/Onion boundaries, vertical slices, DDD, CQRS, event sourcing, event-driven services, microservices, RPC, BFF, serverless, pipelines, microkernels and web/queue/worker systems.
• Compare architecture suitability for a small tool, a domain-rich application or independent services. Ratings are editorial guidance, with features, costs, tradeoffs and references.
• Go deeper into eight clean-code lessons covering naming, interfaces, errors, ownership, configuration, testing, refactoring and SOLID in Go.
• Learn all 23 classic design patterns as Go adaptations and six concurrent patterns, with 53 complete executable examples and 56 design diagrams.
• New topics have separate learning concepts for matching Review and three-choice mistake practice. Existing lesson completion remains recognized.
• Expanded architecture and clean-code explanations cover package boundaries, transactions, failure recovery, tests and gradual migration.

Networking, shell, container and cluster examples remain learning material for your development environment; compiled-program sandbox capabilities are unchanged.
reviewNotes:
GopherForge 1.1.3 build 37. No sign-in or demo credentials required.

This update expands bundled offline learning material. Open Learn, then Go architectures, Clean code in Go, Creational patterns, Structural patterns, Behavioral patterns or Concurrent Go patterns. The architecture unit has a scenario picker and editorial suitability comparison for CLI/tools, domain-rich apps and independent services. Ratings are authored teaching guidance, not performance benchmarks or popularity claims.

The course has 145 teaching lessons in 20 units, including 98 reading lessons, plus 22 prediction challenges. The 53 additional readings provide complete highlighted Go examples, design diagrams, walkthroughs, tradeoffs and primary references. The 27 architecture/clean-code readings have deeper sections on implementation and failure modes. Use Full screen to inspect examples. Reading completion is self-reported and saved; original compiler-judged exercise completion remains compiler-based. Matching Review and three-choice mistake practice use independent concepts for new topics.

The native app compiles Go locally with the bundled Go 1.27.1 toolchain in the existing WebAssembly/WASI sandbox. Networking, native services, Bash, Docker and Kubernetes examples are educational text for the user's development environment, not arbitrary native processes or networking in the sandbox. Projects and progress stay local subject to the chosen Files/iCloud provider. No analytics, advertising, account, subscription or in-app purchase has been added.

Existing iPhone, iPad and supported Duo workspace behavior remains. To check the compiler, create a Worker pool project in Projects, open Build and tap Run; Package with tests demonstrates per-case results. The public website includes the course and support/privacy/terms pages, independently of native learning progress.
